opportunities.title: Subcontractor prequalification and bid-package intake agent
opportunities.problem: Subcontractor qualification and bid intake are two separate manual workflows with no shared record. GWG's contact page routes subs to a standalone 'Submit Subcontractor Application Form' link while client work comes in by phone or web form, and its technology page claims a 'network of vetted vendors' whose vetting is maintained by hand. For an NJ/PA public- and industrial-heavy book, every sub package also has to carry registration and insurance evidence before it can be bid, which is exactly the check a manual inbox does worst.
evidence: Subcontractor onboarding runs through a separate application-form link on the contact page, distinct from the client contact form, so sub qualification and bid intake are separate manual workflows (https://www.gwgllc.com/contact-us/).

Tech page says the firm runs integrated estimating/project-management software that taps 'a network of vetted vendors' and analyzes bids in real time — a vendor list that has to be kept current against insurance, registration and safety status (https://www.gwgllc.com/our-technology/).

Site kiosks already manage subcontractor attendance and safety compliance on site, so sub data lives in at least two places (kiosk/field and office) with no stated link (https://www.gwgllc.com/our-technology/).

NJ public work requires a Public Works Contractor Registration certificate for the contractor and named subcontractors before bidding or working, with fees of $500/year or $750/2 years and a first-violation penalty up to $2,500 — a rules-based check per sub, per package (per the NJDOL FAQ cited in the industry research brief for this run; the statute page itself was not opened in this pass).

Lead Estimator and an EVP whose remit covers estimating, procurement and compliance are both named on the leadership page, so prequalification has owners but competes with bid deadlines (https://www.gwgllc.com/people/).
opportunities.agent_design: Trigger: a sub application form submission, an emailed COI/registration PDF, or a new bid package created in the estimating system. The agent parses the application and attachments, extracts trade codes, insurance limits and expiry dates, W-9 and registration numbers, checks them against the trade's requirements and the project's insurance minimums, dedupes against the existing vendor list, and writes a status record (clear / expiring / missing / lapsed). On the bid side it drafts invitation lists from the scope breakdown, then normalizes returned quotes into a leveling table with a coverage gap list. Human approval gates: a GWG estimator or the Lead Estimator approves any invite list and any vendor marked 'cleared'; a compliance exception (lapsed COI, missing registration) is routed to the EVP whose remit covers procurement and compliance, never auto-approved. Systems touched: website form, shared inbox, file store, estimating/PM system, vendor list.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: It has to read scanned certificates and registration documents, hold an auditable record of when each vendor was cleared and by whom, and write into the estimating system — work a chat subscription cannot do. The compliance decision is consequential (a lapsed COI or missing registration on an NJ public job is a statutory violation), so the agent needs deterministic rules, expiry monitoring and a human sign-off path rather than a prompt.

impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 1 estimator plus part of a coordinator touch each sub package ~20–40 min across intake, document chase and leveling (inference — GWG publishes no bid volume). At roughly 8–20 packages/month that is 3–10 hrs/week, or 150–450 hrs/yr, valued at the NJ cost-estimator wage of $38.74/hr loaded at ~1.3x for payroll taxes and benefits (inference) ≈ $50/hr. Range is deliberately wide because package volume is unconfirmed. Excludes any value from faster quote turnaround or avoided compliance penalties.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3 weeks: one ingestion path (sub application form + emailed COI/registration PDFs), a parsed vendor record with expiry flags, and a bid leveling table covering one live GWG bid package. Success measured as documents touched per sub and hours logged by the estimator before vs during the pilot.

opportunities.title: Preconstruction takeoff and bid-leveling review agent
opportunities.problem: Take-offs, pricing and bid analysis are assigned to a single junior role and sit on the critical path of every proposal. GWG is hiring an Assistant Project Manager whose job is reviewing plans and specs and analyzing take-offs, pricing and bidding, while an open Construction PM role and two 2026 executive hires (CFO, VP Operations) signal the back office is being formalized around a growing project load. Bid documents and sub quotes are commercially sensitive, and a wrong quantity in a fast-track proposal goes straight into margin.
evidence: Assistant PM posting centers on reviewing plans and specs and analyzing take-offs, pricing and bidding — the manual estimating work that consumes junior staff hours (https://www.gwgllc.com/career/assistant-project-manager/).

The firm advertises 3D-model-driven quantity takeoffs and integrated estimating software that analyzes bids in real time, meaning the raw data exists but is stitched into a proposal by hand per job (https://www.gwgllc.com/our-technology/).

Preconstruction is a distinct phase running due diligence, feasibility, programming, permitting and bidding/estimating before handoff to construction — a handoff boundary where numbers get rebuilt (https://www.gwgllc.com/services/).

Vendor self-report (low strength): across 4,000+ US MEP contractors in H1 2026, AI-assisted pre-takeoff saved about 6 hours per estimator per month and estimate comparison fell from 60 to 10 minutes; this is the vendor's own product telemetry with no control group and is directionally useful only (https://www.trimble.com/en/blog/construction/article/actual-results-mep-estimators-ai-assisted-takeoff).

Caution from the research: zero-shot multimodal models were weak on construction hazard recognition (average F1 0.30 across five models, peer-reviewed IAARC conference paper), which argues for constrained, verified agent steps with human sign-off rather than autonomous judgment on site or drawing evidence (https://www.iaarc.org/publications/fulltext/085_How_Reliable_Are_Large_Language_Models__Zero-Shot_Detection_of_Construction_Hazards.pdf).
opportunities.agent_design: Trigger: a new bid invitation or a plan-set revision landing in the estimating queue. The agent builds a trade-by-trade scope checklist from the spec sections, reconciles BIM/model quantities against the estimator's takeoff and flags out-of-tolerance lines for manual recount, normalizes returned subcontractor quotes into a leveling matrix (scope gaps, exclusions, unit-price outliers, alternates), drafts clarification questions for subs and a pre-bid review memo, and assembles the proposal package from GWG's template. Guardrail: the agent never produces or transmits a final bid price — a deterministic spreadsheet computes totals from values the estimator confirms, and every number leaving the firm is approved by the Lead Estimator (or EVP Preconstruction) in a review step logged with the source document. Systems touched: estimating/PM software, BIM model exports, email inbox for sub quotes, document store, proposal templates.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is a multi-document reconciliation job across a model, spec book and dozens of quote PDFs, with arithmetic that must be exact and bid data that cannot go to a consumer chat tool. It needs write access into the estimating system, revision tracking (rev 2 vs rev 1 drawings), and an audit trail showing which quantity came from which sheet — none of which a subscription chatbot provides, and the hazard-recognition evidence above shows why unconstrained model output can't be trusted without a human gate.

impact_estimate.range: $10,000–$25,000 per year of estimator hours, plus reduced recount and leveling rework
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes GWG carries roughly 1 senior/lead estimator plus 1 assistant estimator or coordinator on bids (inference from the named Lead Estimator and the open Assistant PM role) and that 2–4 hrs per estimator per week is recoverable across takeoff cleanup, quote normalization and leveling — about 200–400 hrs/yr at the NJ cost-estimator wage of $38.74/hr loaded at ~1.3x ≈ $50/hr. This is intentionally well below the vendor's claimed 6 hrs/estimator/month plus 83% faster comparison, because no peer-reviewed study measures estimating time savings in a real contractor back office (as the research brief itself notes). Excludes margin protected on bids and change orders (no defensible benchmark found).

opportunities.pilot_scope: 4 weeks on one real bid: agent-generated scope checklist and leveling matrix for a single package, plus a written gap report the estimator scores against their own takeoff. Deliverable includes measured hours per bid and an accuracy log of flagged lines (true gap vs false alarm), which is the evidence needed before touching live pricing.

opportunities.title: Owner's-representative reporting and closeout knowledge agent
opportunities.problem: GWG has moved from single jobs to program-level owner's representation — The Hampshire Companies' New Jersey industrial portfolio — while its published deliverables still include daily logs, progress tracking, video recordings and cost breakdowns generated per project. That is a recurring, template-shaped reporting load per property, on top of PMs who already own schedule creation and coordination from pre-con handoff to closeout. A new CFO and VP Operations are formalizing controls at the same time, and there is no published client portal, so owner reporting is assembled and emailed by hand.
evidence: GWG was selected as owner's representative for The Hampshire Companies' New Jersey industrial portfolio — a multi-property mandate rather than a single job (https://www.gwgllc.com/gwg-news/).

Closeout documentation is described as daily logs, progress tracking, video recordings and cost breakdowns produced from the integrated system — recurring documents with a fixed shape per project (https://www.gwgllc.com/our-technology/).

The PM role owns schedule creation and must coordinate design team, subcontractors, stakeholders and superintendents from pre-construction handoff through closeout, i.e. report production competes with field coordination (https://www.gwgllc.com/career/construction-project-manager/).

CFO (finance) and VP Operations (project launch, resource planning, budgets, forecasting) joined the leadership bench in 2026, a sign controls and reporting are being formalized now (https://www.gwgllc.com/people/).

Site cameras and smart kiosks already generate progress and attendance data, but the site publishes no portal or dashboard for owners to see it themselves — intake is still 'fill out our contact form or call' (https://www.gwgllc.com/contact-us/).
opportunities.agent_design: Two linked behaviours. (1) Reporting: on a weekly trigger per property, the agent pulls progress photos and camera/kiosk data, the schedule and cost tracker, RFI/submittal logs and open issues, then drafts the owner report in GWG's existing template — narrative, variance table, photo sheet, look-ahead — flagging any cost or schedule variance beyond a set threshold. (2) Knowledge: an ask-a-question layer over GWG's own contract, scope exhibits, SOPs and prior reports, so a PM or the VP Operations can get 'what did we commit to on roof warranty at this property' with citations, instead of searching email. Human approval gates: the PM signs off every report before it reaches the owner; the CFO approves any financial figure; the agent never sends to an owner contact directly. Systems touched: PM/estimating system, cost tracker, camera and kiosk feeds, document store, email.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: It requires authenticated access to several internal systems plus camera feeds, per-property permission scoping (owners must not see each other's data), and document production that stands up as a contractual record. Answer quality has to be traceable to a clause or a log entry, not generated prose; a chatbot subscription offers no audit trail, no system write-back and no data-residency control over owner and contract data.

impact_estimate.range: $9,000–$25,000 per year of PM/coordinator time, plus faster owner-report turnaround
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 4–8 active projects/properties (inference from a 12-project public portfolio plus a multi-property owner mandate) and 2–5 hrs/week saved in aggregate across report assembly, photo culling and document lookups, i.e. 100–260 hrs/yr at the NJ construction-manager wage of $66.46/hr loaded at ~1.3x ≈ $86/hr. The low end reflects that report templates may already be partly automated in GWG's PM software. The turnaround/win-rate upside on owner's-rep pursuits is an inference, not quantified, and is excluded from the range.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3 weeks on one property: auto-drafted weekly owner report (narrative + variance table + photo sheet) generated from existing data, plus a knowledge Q&A over that project's contract, scope exhibit and prior reports with citations. Measured as PM minutes per report and accuracy of variance flags reviewed by the VP Operations.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (19/30): several concrete operational signals — a standalone sub application form beside a phone/web-form-only intake, two open PM-track roles, a named Lead Estimator, a program-level owner mandate with per-property reporting, and 2026 CFO/VP Ops hires formalizing controls. But none of it is quantified by an independent source: no reviews were retrievable, no headcount or revenue is published, and the pain is inferred from how the site and job posts are structured. Fit (17/20): strong. GWG already runs BIM takeoffs, integrated estimating and site cameras, and its Chief Administrative & Technology Officer's remit explicitly covers IT and business-process optimization — an internal sponsor who understands integration, plus adjacent systems for an agent to sit between. Ability to pay (12/20): mid-size regional design-build firm with a 140,000 sq ft life-sciences project, a multi-property owner mandate and a CFO on staff, but size and revenue are unconfirmed and a lean back office may cap budget. Ease (11/15): single Edison office, named decision makers, and pilots can run on one live bid or one property — though bid deadlines are erratic and the historical estimating/bid workflow may be partly undocumented. Strategic (12/15): sub prequalification, bid leveling and owner reporting are near-identical across NJ/NY design-build and CM firms, so a working build here is a repeatable industry product rather than a one-off. Held below 75 because every opportunity currently rests on the firm's own website and job postings, with no independent corroboration and no measured baseline.

best_evidence_signal: GWG's own Assistant PM posting assigns plan/spec review, take-offs, pricing and bid analysis to one junior role while the firm advertises real-time bid analysis and 3D takeoffs — the manual-vs-tooling gap is visible in its own words (https://www.gwgllc.com/career/assistant-project-manager/).
suggested_channel: email to Eric Korb, Chief Administrative & Technology Officer (remit covers IT, finance and business-process optimization), with a short note to Eric Gatti, President | CEO — LinkedIn as a secondary touch; a walk-in to the Edison office is viable given the firm is an active Edison Chamber member, but email gives Korb something concrete to forward internally
data_gaps: No independent customer or employee reviews were retrievable (Google, Yelp, BBB, Glassdoor, Indeed, ZipRecruiter all blocked automated access), so pain evidence rests on the firm's own site, its careers pages and the Edison Chamber listing.
Employee headcount, revenue, bid volume and active project count are all unpublished; every impact range therefore states its volume assumption explicitly and uses wide ranges.

No named CRM, ERP, estimating product or client portal is disclosed, so the 'systems touched' sections describe generic categories (estimating/PM system, cost tracker, document store) rather than verified products.

Web search providers were rate-limited during this run, so only the two wage benchmark pages were confirmed by direct fetch (O*NET local wages for Cost Estimators 13-1051 and Construction Managers 11-9021, BLS May 2025 data); the NJ contractor-registration detail is taken from the industry brief's NJDOL entry and was not re-fetched against a primary page.

No peer-reviewed study measures time saved or error reduction for estimating, bid leveling, subcontractor prequalification or owner reporting in an operating contractor; the only quantified time-savings figures are vendor self-reports (Trimble, Togal) and are treated as low-strength and deliberately discounted.

The hazard-recognition studies in the industry brief are image-task research and are used here only as a caution about unconstrained model output; they do not measure back-office workflow value. The arXiv chain-of-thought prompting item is a working paper (preprint), not peer-reviewed, and is not relied on for any estimate.
